# F1 glossary

## Aerodynamics & car setup

**Downforce** — the aerodynamic force pushing a car down onto the track, generated by wings and the floor. More downforce means more grip in corners at the cost of top speed on straights.

**DRS (Drag Reduction System)** — a flap on the rear wing that opens to reduce drag on straights. A driver can only activate it when within one second of the car ahead at a detection point, and only inside designated DRS zones, from the third lap of the race onward (disabled for the first two laps and in wet or unsafe conditions).

**Parc fermé** — the period from the start of qualifying until the race begins, during which teams are barred from making significant setup changes to the car. Only very limited adjustments (like tyre pressures within a set range, or repairs) are allowed; anything more forces a driver to start from the pit lane.

## Tyres & strategy

**Undercut** — pitting earlier than a rival to get onto fresh tyres sooner, hoping the pace advantage of new rubber lets you pass them once they eventually pit themselves.

**Overcut** — the opposite: staying out longer than a rival on older tyres, gaining track position because your rival loses time in the pits while you keep circulating.

**Tyre degradation** — the rate at which a tyre loses grip and pace over a stint, caused by wear (rubber physically grinding away) and thermal degradation (overheating breaking down the rubber's structure).

**Graining / blistering** — two different tyre degradation failure modes. Graining happens when the tyre surface shears rather than grips, usually at lower temperatures; blistering is small pockets of gas forming under the surface at high temperatures. Both reduce grip.

## Race control & flags

**Blue flag** — shown to a driver about to be lapped, instructing them to let the faster car through; ignoring it repeatedly can result in a penalty.

**Safety car (SC)** — a physical car deployed onto the track that bunches the whole field up behind it at reduced speed, used for serious incidents needing the track partially or fully controlled.

**Virtual safety car (VSC)** — a lighter-touch version of the above: no physical car appears, but all drivers must stay under a set delta time until it ends, used for less severe incidents.

## Qualifying & race formats

**Q1 / Q2 / Q3** — the three knockout stages of a standard qualifying session. The slowest cars are eliminated after Q1 and Q2; the remaining ten fight for pole position in Q3.

**Grid penalty** — a penalty (for a rules breach, or for exceeding a power unit component allocation) that moves a driver back a set number of places on the starting grid, applied after qualifying positions are set.

**Sprint** — a shorter, standalone race held on the Saturday of select race weekends, awarding a reduced points scale to the top eight finishers, separate from the main Grand Prix.
